findings.description: The Lambda function's environment variables contain hardcoded plaintext AWS credentials (access_key = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE" and secret_key = "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"). These are committed to source control and readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, so the credentials must be treated as compromised and rotated immediately; secrets should come from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store via the execution role.
The function uses runtime "nodejs12.x", which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities unpatched in a function that holds credentials.

The role has no permissions boundary and no attached policy documented at all, while the function embeds long-lived static credentials in its environment; without a boundary or scoped permissions defined in code, effective permissions cannot be constrained or audited per the least-privilege guidance.
